## What Is an Option Trading App?


An option trading app is software that helps you analyse, test or place options trades. You may also see these tools called options apps or options trading software. Most fall into one of three groups, and a few cover more than one.


-


Broker apps hold your trading account and send your orders to the exchange.


-


Analytics platforms, including option chain apps, help you read open interest, Greeks, volatility and payoff.


-


Testing and automation platforms let you backtest rules on past data, practise in a simulator and run strategies through a connected broker.


Many traders use one app from each group. That is why this guide compares apps by the job they do, not by a single score.

## Options Trading Platforms for Analysis and Testing


These five options trading platforms help you research or test a strategy before you trade it. Some of them can also place orders through a connected broker.


### 1. AlgoTest: Best for Backtesting, Practice and Options Automation


AlgoTest brings strategy building, testing and execution into one workflow. It fits traders who want to check an idea on past data before any real money goes in.


Each tool answers a different question:


-


The backtester runs your entry, exit and risk rules on historical data and reports drawdown, win rate and trade-level P&L.


-


The Option Simulator replays a past session so you can watch premiums, Greeks and P&L change as you manage a position.


-


The Strategy Builder lets you build multi-leg positions from the option chain and see payoff, Greeks and margin before you trade.


-


Paper trading runs a strategy on live market data with simulated orders.


-


Signals AI lets you build and test indicator-based strategies without writing code.


[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/register?utm_source=blogs&utm_medium=organics&utm_campaign=seo&utm_source=blogs&utm_medium=organics&utm_campaign=seo) covers NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY, SENSEX, BANKEX and stock options.[MCX commodity options](https://algotest.in/blog/mcx-options-trading) can now be backtested as well. Tested strategies can run live through supported brokers.


**Pricing:** Every account gets 100 free backtests a month. Credit packs start at ₹499 for 500 credits. Paper trading and live deployment use credits per strategy for each 28-day cycle.


**Check before choosing:** Data coverage varies by instrument and tool. A manual simulator session does not turn into an algo on its own, so you still need to set the rules in the backtester or Strategy Builder.


**Best for:** Traders who want to move from an idea to a tested, automated strategy.


> **Planning a multi-leg trade?** Build it in the[Strategy Builder](https://algotest.in/feature/strategy-builder?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=strategy-builder&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=strategy-builder) and check payoff, Greeks and margin before you place it.


### 2. Opstra by Definedge: Best for Volatility and OI Research


Opstra is an options analytics platform from Definedge. It covers option chains, open interest, PCR, implied volatility, volatility skew and surface, a strategy builder and a simulator.


Backtesting sits in the Pro plan and runs on end-of-day data. Pro access is tied to a Definedge account, and orders go through the Definedge ecosystem.


**Pricing:** The basic plan is free but limited, and live data sits behind Pro. Check the current Pro terms before you rely on its backtests.


**Check before choosing:** Make sure end-of-day testing matches how you trade. Intraday rules need a tool that tests at a finer interval.


**Best for:** Traders who need detailed OI and volatility research.


Related:[AlgoTest vs Opstra](https://algotest.in/blog/algotest-vs-opstra/) |[Opstra vs Sensibull](https://algotest.in/blog/opstra-vs-sensibull/)


### 3. StockMock: Best for Dedicated Backtesting and Replay


StockMock focuses on testing. It offers multi-year options backtests, a simulator, a strategy builder and charts.


Its plans are split by function. The Analytics plan covers the simulator, builder and charts. The Backtesting plan covers multi-year backtests.


**Pricing:** StockMock lists Analytics at ₹349 for 30 days and Backtesting at ₹449 for 7 days. Longer plans are available.


**Check before choosing:** An Analytics plan does not include multi-year backtests, so add up both plans if you need both. StockMock does not place live trades, so you will need a separate route to execution.


**Best for:** Traders whose main need is historical options testing.


Related:[StockMock vs AlgoTest Option Simulator](https://algotest.in/blog/stockmock-vs-algotest-option-simulator/)


### 4. Quantsapp: Best for Deep Options Analytics With Broker Trading


Quantsapp offers live Greeks, OI analytics, backtesting tools, alerts and a large library of learning content. You can add your broker inside Quantsapp and manage trades from its screen, so it is more than a research tool.


**Pricing:** Quantsapp has a free tier and paid tiers. Some execution and API features have their own access conditions.


**Check before choosing:** Confirm which backtesting tools and order types your plan includes before you subscribe.


**Best for:** Traders who want deep options research and order placement in one place.


Related:[AlgoTest vs Quantsapp](https://algotest.in/blog/algotest-vs-quantsapp/)


### 5. Strike Money: Best for Scanners and Wider Market Context


Strike Money combines market scanners, heatmaps, relative rotation graphs, sentiment tools and FII/DII data with derivatives analytics. Its options tools include the option chain, OI insights, max pain and a strategy builder with payoff charts.


Strike’s own pages list backtesting among its strategy tools. It does not place orders, so you will still need a broker to trade.


**Pricing:** Strike lists a one-month plan at about ₹650, with discounts on longer plans.


**Check before choosing:** If historical testing matters to you, check how deep and flexible its backtests are before you depend on them.


**Best for:** Traders who read options activity alongside the wider market.


> **Want free option chain data first?** Track OI, PCR and max pain on AlgoTest’s[Nifty option chain](https://algotest.in/nifty-option-chain) and[Sensex option chain](https://algotest.in/sensex-option-chain) .


### Broker Apps for Options Trading


A broker app holds your trading account and sends your orders to the exchange. All four brokers below charge ₹20 per executed options order on their standard plans. The real differences are in tools, account charges and how you like to trade.


### 6. Zerodha Kite + Sensibull: Best for Visual Strategy Analysis on Zerodha


Kite handles your Zerodha account and orders. Sensibull adds options tools on top, including a strategy builder, payoff charts, Greeks, an option chain and Draft Portfolios for tracking hypothetical trades.


**Pricing:** Zerodha charges a flat ₹20 per executed options order. This rises to ₹40 in two cases: if your account has a debit balance, or if you don’t keep the required cash share of your F&O margin and the shortfall exceeds ₹5 lakh. Sensibull Pro is ₹0 a month for Zerodha users, while users of other brokers pay for Pro.


**Check before choosing:** Sensibull does not offer historical backtesting, and Draft Portfolios track live prices only. Test rule-based ideas on past data with a separate tool.


**Best for:** Zerodha users who want visual strategy analysis for manual trading.


Readers Also Liked:[12 Best Sensibull Alternatives in India](https://algotest.in/blog/sensibull-alternatives-india/)


### 7. Upstox: Best for Chart-Led Trading With a Built-In Strategy Builder


Upstox pairs its trading account with charts, an option chain and a strategy builder. You can pick strikes from the option chain, view the payoff and place a multi-leg strategy order in one flow.


Pro Web also supports basket orders of up to 20 orders. Sensibull can be connected to an Upstox account, though Pro is paid for non-Zerodha users.


**Pricing:** Upstox charges a flat ₹20 per executed options order. New customers get zero AMC in the first year. Taxes and exchange charges are extra.


**Check before choosing:** Upstox does not offer native backtesting or paper trading.


**Best for:** Traders who want chart-based decisions and options execution in one broker app.


Related:[Does Upstox Support Backtesting?](https://algotest.in/blog/does-upstox-platform-support-backtesting-or-not/)


### 8. Angel One: Best for Options Trading Alongside Investing


Angel One brings trading, investing and research into one app. Its F&O screens give you the option chain, charts and indicators next to the rest of your portfolio.


**Pricing:** Angel One charges ₹20 per executed F&O order. New accounts pay no brokerage up to ₹500 in the first 30 days, after which the standard rate applies.


**Check before choosing:** Research tools and an order screen do not replace testing your own entry, exit and risk rules.


**Best for:** Traders who prefer one broad broker app over separate tools.


Related:[Best Brokers for Algo Trading in India](https://algotest.in/blog/best-brokers-for-algo-trading-in-india/)


### 9. Dhan Options Trader: Best for an Options-Focused Order Screen


Dhan offers a separate Options Trader app and web platform built for F&O traders. Its strategy builder lets you create, analyse and execute multi-leg positions, with TradingView charts available in the same ecosystem.


**Pricing:** Dhan charges ₹20 per executed options order, with ₹0 account opening and ₹0 AMC for individual and HUF accounts.


**Check before choosing:** A payoff view at selected prices is not a historical backtest, and Dhan does not offer native backtesting.


**Best for:** Active options traders who want strategy analysis and execution in one broker interface.

These are standard rates from each broker’s official schedule, checked on 3 November 2026. Account-specific plans and offers can differ.


Take an[iron condor](https://algotest.in/blog/iron-condor-strategy/) . It has four legs, so opening and closing it takes eight executed orders.


8 orders × ₹20 = ₹160 in brokerage alone.


Adjustments, re-entries and order slicing add more orders. STT, exchange charges, GST, stamp duty and slippage come on top, so ₹20 per order is never ₹20 for the whole strategy.


Before you place a multi-leg trade, check how much margin it will block with the[margin calculator](https://algotest.in/margin-calculator) .

## Backtesting, Simulator or Paper Trading: Which Do You Need?


Tool


What it shows you


Main limit


Strategy builder (payoff)


How a position’s P&L changes with price and time


It is a projection, not evidence from past data


Rule-based backtester


How fixed entry, exit and risk rules performed on historical data


Results depend on the data, costs and rules you set


Historical simulator


How you would manage a trade while replaying a past session


Knowing what happened later can bias your choices


Paper trading (forward testing)


How a strategy behaves on live market data


Simulated fills can differ from real ones


Start by choosing an[options strategy](https://algotest.in/blog/options-trading-strategies/) that fits your market view. Then check its payoff and replay a few past sessions in an[options simulator](https://algotest.in/blog/best-options-simulator-india/) . After that, backtest the fixed rules over a longer period and paper trade them on live data before you use real money.


> **Have clear entry and exit rules?**[Backtest them on AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/feature/backtest) and review drawdown, trading costs and trade-level results.

### FAQs


#### Which is the best option trading app in India?


It depends on what you need. AlgoTest suits backtesting, practice and automation. Zerodha Kite with Sensibull, Upstox, Angel One and Dhan suit manual trading from a broker account. Opstra, StockMock, Quantsapp and Strike Money focus on research and testing.


#### Which trading app is best in India for options traders?


For placing options trades, Zerodha, Upstox, Angel One and Dhan all charge ₹20 per executed options order, so choose by tools and interface. For testing and automating a strategy, pair your broker with a platform like AlgoTest.


#### Which option trading app is best for beginners?


Look for clear payoff charts, simple order screens and a way to practise before using real money. AlgoTest’s Option Simulator lets you replay past sessions, while Sensibull’s Draft Portfolios track hypothetical trades on live prices.


A simple app does not remove the risk of options trading.


#### Is there a free options trading app in India?


Yes, several apps have free tiers. AlgoTest offers 100 free backtests a month and a free Option Simulator, Sensibull Pro is free for Zerodha users, and Opstra and Quantsapp have free basic plans.


Brokerage, taxes and exchange charges still apply to live trades.


#### Which option trading apps offer backtesting?


AlgoTest, StockMock and Opstra (on its Pro plan) offer historical options backtesting. Quantsapp includes backtesting tools depending on the plan, and Strike Money also lists backtesting among its tools.


Sensibull and the broker apps in this list focus on payoff analysis rather than historical backtests.


#### Is Sensibull free?


Sensibull Pro is free for Zerodha users. Users of other brokers get a limited free plan and pay for Pro.


#### What is the difference between a broker app and an options analytics platform?


A broker app holds your trading account and places orders on the exchange. An analytics platform helps you research or test a strategy.


Some platforms connect to your broker to place orders, but that does not make them your broker.


#### Can I practise options trading without a broker account?


Yes. You can replay past sessions in AlgoTest’s Option Simulator without connecting a broker.


To place real trades, you need a broker account with the F&O segment enabled.


#### Do I need a separate option chain app?


Not usually. Every broker app in this guide includes an option chain, and analytics platforms add OI, PCR and max pain views. You can also track these for free on AlgoTest’s Nifty and Sensex option chains.


#### Is a strategy builder the same as backtesting?


No. A strategy builder shows a position’s projected payoff. Backtesting runs fixed rules on historical data to show how they would have performed.


#### How much brokerage do option trading apps charge in India?


Zerodha, Upstox, Angel One and Dhan each charge ₹20 per executed options order on their standard plans. A four-leg strategy opened and closed costs ₹160 in brokerage before taxes and other charges.
